summary: Fix three camera-related dead ends found while live-benching the setup wizard. (1) Picking any stock detection model in the wizard's AI step, including reverting to the default, always failed with 'model file not found': the model picker stripped the '.pt' suffix off each option before POSTing, but the server only matched full file names, so the request fell through to the 'custom local path' branch. `canonicalStockModel` in `training_runner.go` now accepts either form, and the picker sends the name the API lists; applying a model also no longer re-runs the whole step's multi-second Python-runtime probe before showing the new 'Current' value, which previously left the old model's name on screen under a toast saying the new one was set. (2) Camera discovery (the wizard's 'Add your first camera' step and the Cameras -> Discover screen) reported a bare 'internal server Error' whenever it found no camera, on any host with at least one network adapter that cannot carry a multicast probe (VirtualBox host-only, WSL/Hyper-V vEthernet, a link-local 169.254.x fallback) - i.e. most developer and many production machines. `infra/onvif.Discover` now fails only when every listener it opened failed to send at all; finding zero devices, or having one deaf adapter among working ones, is reported as a normal empty result, and a genuine failure carries its reason instead of a hidden 500. (3) Camera credential changes were never reaching the audit trail: `NewCameraApi` accepted an `Auditor` argument but never assigned it to the handler struct, so every camera audit call silently hit a nil Auditor. It is now wired like every sibling API.
compatibility: Backward-compatible; no schema, config, or API-shape change. Existing installs get a working stock-model picker and honest discovery errors on their next update with no action needed. Camera credential changes made before this fix were never recorded in the audit trail and cannot be recovered retroactively; changes made after this fix are recorded going forward.
